fields.default: How a house gets built, in six questions

fields.name: intro
fields.label: Intro
fields.default: Ines Morel, founding partner of Morel Okafor Architects in Bath, on fees, planning and why the first meeting should cost nothing.

fields.name: pullQuote
fields.label: Pull quote
fields.default: A good brief is two pages long and mostly about how you live.

itemFields.name: answer
itemFields.label: Answer
itemFields.default: Yes, within about an hour's drive, so we can be on site every fortnight.

default.question: When should someone first call an architect?
default.answer: Before they buy, if they can. Half an hour on a plot or in a tired house can save a client from the wrong purchase. We make that first visit for free.

default.question: How do your fees work?
default.answer: For a full service we charge 9 to 12 percent of the build cost, split across five stages. You can stop after any stage and keep the drawings.

default.question: How long does planning permission take?
default.answer: The council has eight weeks to decide a household application. Allow three months before that for surveys and design, and longer for a listed building.

default.question: Do you help to find a builder?
default.answer: We tender every project to three or four contractors we have worked with before, then check their prices line by line. The choice is always the client's.

default.question: What sends a project over budget?
default.answer: Changing your mind on site. A wall moved on paper costs nothing. A wall moved in week twelve costs £4,000. We settle the decisions before the digger arrives.

default.question: Is any job too small for you?
default.answer: We take on a few extensions and loft conversions each year, from about £80,000 of building work. Below that, we will happily recommend someone good.
